concepts.title: Medical terminology — definition
body: It is the language used to precisely describe the human body including its components, processes, conditions affecting it, and procedures performed upon it.
Medical terminology is used in the field of medicine and pharmacy.
concepts.ar: لغة بتوصف جسم الإنسان بدقة: مكوناته، العمليات اللي بتحصل فيه، الحالات اللي بتأثر عليه، والإجراءات اللي بتتعمل عليه.

concepts.title: Word parts & origin
body: Most medical terms are a combination of word parts: prefix, root (stem), suffix.
Most of them come from Latin or Greek words.
Other languages such as English, German and French.

concepts.title: The word parts
body: Root: the word part that is the core of the word.
Prefix: a word part attached to the beginning of a word root to modify its meaning.
Suffix: a word part attached to the end of the word root to modify its meaning.
Combining vowel: a word part, usually an “o” or “i”.
concepts.ar: الـ Root هو قلب الكلمة. الـ prefix في الأول والـ suffix في الآخر، والاتنين بيعدّلوا المعنى.

concepts.title: Defining medical terms through word structural analysis
body: You can define a term according to word structure analysis by: prefix, root, suffix.
Patterns on the slides: Root + suffix (lipemia) · Prefix + root + suffix (hyperlipemia) · Root + combining vowel + suffix (carcinogen).
concepts.ar: عشان تعرّف أي term: قسّمه prefix / root / suffix وهات معنى كل جزء.

concepts.title: Combining vowels
body: [o] is the most common combining vowel; [i] is the second most common.
When a medical term has more than one root, each is joined by a vowel.
They are used to join: (i) root to root, (ii) root to suffix.
Why? To ease pronunciation.
Is their presence mandatory? No — not all medical terms have combining vowels.
Additional roots: often a medical term is formed of two or more roots (hyper/lip/o/protein/emia).
concepts.ar: o الأشهر وبعدها i. بتربط root بـ root أو root بـ suffix، ومش إجبارية.

concepts.title: Formation of medical terms
body: All medical terms build from the root.
Prefixes and suffixes are attached to the root to modify its meaning.
Often two or more roots are linked before being modified.

concepts.title: Color code for medical terminology
body: Prefix- (blue): meaning before the root · modifies the meaning · e.g. hyper-, hypo-, anti-, pre-
-Root- (green): main meaning of the term · usually indicates the organ, system or action · e.g. cardi-, nephro-, hepat-, gastr-
-Suffix (pink): meaning after the root · indicates condition, procedure, disease, drug class, etc. · e.g. -itis, -emia, -ology, -logy, -ase

concepts.title: Suffixes
body: Suffixes are the ending part of medical terms.
Suffixes tend to bring an action to the medical terms.
Medical suffixes can be categorized into: specialties, condition of, disease, small, surgery, adjective suffix.
concepts.ar: الـ suffix آخر الكلمة وبيدّيها action.

concepts.title: Disease — definition
body: A condition of a person, animal, or plant in which its body or structure is harmed because an organ or part is unable to work as it usually does.

concepts.title: Adjective suffix — definition
body: A suffix added to a root word to form an adjective.

concepts.title: Competency (intro slide)
body: It is a set of characteristics including knowledge, skills and attitude. All are integrated within a situation which takes place in a setting.
Consists of a description of the essential skills, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors required for effective performance of a real-world task or activity (Mrowicki, 1986).
الجدارات = Knowledge + Skills + Behaviors + Attitudes · الكفاءات = القدرة على توظيف هذه العناصر في الأداء الفعلي

concepts.title: Grading system
body: Class activity / periodicals (25 marks): mid-term / quiz = 20 marks · research = 5 marks
Practical exam: (-) marks
Lecture attendance & behavior: bonus = 2 to 3 marks
Final written exam = 75 marks
Memorizing and spelling basic medical word components are the first steps for learning how to form medical terms.
The next step is to construct the words using the following steps (rules).

rules.rule: A combining vowel is used to join root to root as well as to any suffix beginning with a consonant.
rules.example: electr/o/cardi/o/gram — electrical record of the heart
rules.ar: o بين root وroot، وقبل أي suffix بيبدأ بـ consonant.

rules.rule: A combining vowel is not used before a suffix that begins with a vowel.
rules.example: vas + ectomy → vasectomy — excision of a vessel
rules.ar: الـ suffix بيبدأ بـ vowel؟ يبقى مفيش o.

rules.rule: If the root ends in a vowel and the suffix begins with the same vowel, drop the final vowel from the root and do not use a combining vowel.
rules.example: cardi + itis → carditis — inflammation of heart
rules.ar: نفس الحرف مرتين؟ شيل حرف الـ root.

rules.rule: When a prefix ends in a vowel and the root begins with a vowel, the final vowel is dropped from the prefix.
rules.example: para + enter + al → parenteral — pertaining to alongside of the intestine
rules.ar: هنا اللي بيتشال حرف الـ prefix مش الـ root.

rules.rule: Most often a combining vowel is inserted between two roots even when the second root begins with a vowel.
rules.example: cardi/o/esophag/eal — pertaining to heart and esophagus
rules.ar: بين two roots حط o حتى لو التاني بيبدأ بـ vowel.
